title: Cohomology on a qcqs object commutes with bounded-below filtered colimits
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use its small pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on this site, and let $U$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated object (its underlying scheme has a finite affine open cover, and intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact). Let $I$ be a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], let $a\in\mathbf Z$, and let $(K_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ be a diagram of cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of sheaves of left $\mathcal R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $K_i^b=0$ for every $i$ and $b<a$. Colimits of these complexes are taken termwise in sheaves of $\mathcal R$-modules. Write $H^q(U,L^\bullet)=H^q(R\Gamma(U,L^\bullet))$ for hypercohomology, where $R\Gamma(U,-)$ is computed by evaluating a bounded-below injective resolution at $U$, with values in complexes of abelian groups. Then for every $q\in\mathbf Z$ the canonical map induced by the colimit cocone is an isomorphism:
$$
\varinjlim_{i\in I}H^q(U,K_i^\bullet)\longrightarrow H^q\bigl(U,\varinjlim_{i\in I}K_i^\bullet\bigr).
$$

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], the category of left module sheaves over the arbitrary ring sheaf $\mathcal R$ on our small site has all small colimits. Form $K^b=\varinjlim_i K_i^b$ in sheaves of $\mathcal R$-modules, with cocone maps $\iota_i^b$. The chain-map identities for the transition maps make the maps $\iota_i^{b+1}d_i^b$ a cocone, hence define $d^b:K^b\to K^{b+1}$ uniquely by $d^b\iota_i^b=\iota_i^{b+1}d_i^b$. The composites $d^{b+1}d^b$ vanish after all $\iota_i^b$, so vanish by the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Thus these data give the termwise colimit complex. For $b<a$ the diagram is zero and its colimit is zero: maps from its zero cocone to any object are unique. Consequently $K^b=0$ below the same $a$.

source.place: Opening sentence: termwise colimit and its common lower bound

proof.text: By clause 3 of [det-pe-hypercover-existence], choose one hypercover $W_\bullet\to U$ whose terms are affine and weakly contractible; it is fixed throughout the diagram. Apply [det-pe-hypercover-complex] to every $K_i^\bullet$ and to $K^\bullet$, using their common lower bound. Put $T_i=\operatorname{Tot}(K_i^b(W_r))$ and $T=\operatorname{Tot}(K^b(W_r))$. This gives natural isomorphisms $\eta_i:H^q(U,K_i^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(T_i)$ and $\eta:H^q(U,K^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(T)$. For every integer $n$, $T_i^n=\bigoplus_{0\le r\le n-a}K_i^{n-r}(W_r)$ and $T^n=\bigoplus_{0\le r\le n-a}K^{n-r}(W_r)$. These sums are finite and are zero when $n<a$.

source.place: Fix one hypercover; natural hypercover calculation and formula for the finite total degrees

proof.text: For each $r,b$, apply [det-pe-sections-limits-colimits] with $W=W_r$ to the diagram of sheaves $K_i^b$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\alpha_{r,b}:\varinjlim_i K_i^b(W_r)\xrightarrow{\sim}K^b(W_r)$ induced by the maps $\iota_i^b(W_r)$. To justify passage to underlying abelian groups, put $A=\varinjlim_i K_i^b(W_r)$ in abelian groups with legs $j_i$. For each $s\in\mathcal R(W_r)$, the compatible additive maps $x\mapsto j_i(sx)$ induce an additive endomorphism $\mu_s$ of $A$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Precomposing with all $j_i$ proves $\mu_{s+t}=\mu_s+\mu_t$, $\mu_{st}=\mu_s\mu_t$, and $\mu_1=1$, so $s\cdot x=\mu_s(x)$ makes $A$ a left module; the additive map induced by any compatible linear cocone is linear, again by testing on all $j_i$. Thus $A$ is also the module colimit, and the underlying abelian-group comparison $\alpha_{r,b}$ is an isomorphism. Each $\iota_i$ is a morphism of module sheaves, hence commutes with restriction along every face map $W_{r+1}\to W_r$; and step 1 gives $d^b\iota_i^b=\iota_i^{b+1}d_i^b$. Therefore the $\alpha_{r,b}$ commute with the horizontal alternating face sums and the vertical differentials $(-1)^rd^b$.

source.place: Sectionwise colimit comparison on every hypercover term; compatibility with faces and complex differentials

proof.text: For fixed $n$ let $S_n=\{r\in\mathbf Z:0\le r\le n-a\}$. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and the coproduct property give $\varinjlim_i\bigoplus_{r\in S_n}K_i^{n-r}(W_r)\cong\bigoplus_{r\in S_n}\varinjlim_iK_i^{n-r}(W_r)$: a map from either side to an abelian group $B$ is precisely a family of maps $K_i^{n-r}(W_r)\to B$ compatible in $i$, one for each $r$. Composing with $\bigoplus_r\alpha_{r,n-r}$ gives an isomorphism $\beta^n:\varinjlim_iT_i^n\to T^n$ whose composite with each cocone map is the total map induced by $\iota_i$. These maps commute with differentials: on the $(i,r)$ summand both composites are the sum of $\sum_j(-1)^j d_j^*\iota_i^{n-r}$ and $(-1)^r d_K^{n-r}\iota_i^{n-r}$, equal respectively to $\sum_j(-1)^j\iota_i^{n-r}d_j^*$ and $(-1)^r\iota_i^{n-r+1}d_i^{n-r}$ by step 3. Hence $\beta:\varinjlim_iT_i\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ is an isomorphism of complexes, where the colimit differential is induced degreewise as in step 1. The argument includes $S_n=\varnothing$.

source.place: Finite direct sums commute with colimits; differentials are induced by the same face maps and differentials

proof.text: For every $n$ write $Z_i^n=\ker(d_{T_i}^n)$, $B_i^n=\operatorname{im}(d_{T_i}^{n-1})$, and $H_i^n=Z_i^n/B_i^n$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Chain maps preserve cycles and boundaries, so the sequences $0\to Z_i^n\to T_i^n\to B_i^{n+1}\to0$ and $0\to B_i^n\to Z_i^n\to H_i^n\to0$ are compatible diagrams of short exact sequences. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact], their colimits are short exact. Thus $\varinjlim B_i^n\to\varinjlim Z_i^n\to\varinjlim T_i^n$ consists of injections, and the differential of $\varinjlim T_i$ factors as the surjection $\varinjlim T_i^n\to\varinjlim B_i^{n+1}$ followed by its injection into $\varinjlim T_i^{n+1}$. Its kernel is therefore $\varinjlim Z_i^n$ and its image in degree $n$ is $\varinjlim B_i^n$. The second short exact sequence then identifies $\varinjlim H_i^n$ with $H^n(\varinjlim T_i)$. This identification sends a cocone image of a cycle class to the class of the cocone image of that cycle, so it is the canonical comparison $\gamma:\varinjlim_iH^q(T_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(\varinjlim_iT_i)$. Compose with $H^q(\beta)$ from step 4. No boundedness hypothesis is needed for this algebraic step.

source.place: Filtered colimits of abelian groups are exact, so cohomology commutes with them

proof.text: Let $\lambda_i:T_i\to\varinjlim_jT_j$ be the colimit legs. Naturality in [det-pe-hypercover-complex], applied to $\iota_i:K_i\to K$, gives $\eta\circ H^q(U,\iota_i)=H^q(\beta\lambda_i)\circ\eta_i$. By step 5 the composite $\eta^{-1}\circ H^q(\beta)\circ\gamma\circ(\varinjlim_i\eta_i)$ is an isomorphism, and precomposing it with the $i$-th colimit leg gives exactly $H^q(U,\iota_i)$. The uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] therefore identifies this composite with the canonical map in the statement. This proves the assertion for all $q\in\mathbf Z$, including $q<a$.

source.place: Final sentence: naturality identifies the constructed isomorphism with the canonical map

No new nodes. Second reading constructs the scalar action on the underlying abelian-group colimit and checks its module universal property.
